answer_1.quote: We tackle the problem of long document extractive summarization by combining two essential tasks of section segmentation and sentence extraction.
answer_1.outputs: extractive summaries consisting of selected sentences from the source document

answer_2.quote: Standard evaluation metrics (ROUGE; , including R-1, R-2 and R-L, are used to measure the quality of system summaries.

answer_4.quote: We performed evaluation using Amazon Mechanical Turk on 100 randomly selected summarization instances from arXiv.
answer_4.guideline: We focus on evaluating informativeness and diversity of summary sentences. For informativeness, we take the union of summary sentences and ask human evaluators to judge the relevance of each sentence against the ground-truth summary on a scale of 1 (worst) to 5 (best). For diversity, we obtain the symmetric difference of two summaries and ask humans to judge if each sentence has offered new content different from those of the common sentences.
